title: QA_Platform_started_round_cannot_be_rescheduled_clock_unchanged
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ whose bidding started when it was published (about 20 minutes open), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to move the round to start in one hour and end in two hours.
2. Read the round back.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'. The round still starts in the past and ends at its original time.
rationale: Moving a live round's start would close bidding under vendors who are quoting; the refusal must also leave the clock untouched.

title: QA_Platform_started_round_reversed_window_refused_by_started_rule
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to reschedule with an end time one hour BEFORE the new start time.
expectedResult: Refused by the 'already started' rule, which runs before any time check: HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.
rationale: Shows the guard order: a started round answers 258 whatever the times are (the reschedule path itself has no end-after-start check, see API-EVDTME-018).

title: QA_Platform_started_round_text_times_refused_without_crash
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer sends a reschedule whose start and end are words instead of times.
expectedResult: Refused cleanly before the text reaches the time conversion: HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!' (never a 500).
rationale: On an upcoming round the same text crashes in Time.at (API-EVDTME-023); on a started round the 258 guard must come first.

title: QA_Platform_only_new_start_time_is_silently_ignored
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer sends only a new start time (one hour from now), no end time.
2. Read the round back.
expectedResult: Expected (today): HTTP 200 and nothing changes — the reschedule branch needs BOTH times, so the request falls through to a generic save. The round still starts in the past. Should be refused (code 2) so the caller knows nothing happened.
rationale: A silent 200 tells an integration or a stale screen that the reschedule worked when it did not.

title: QA_Platform_only_new_end_time_does_not_extend_round
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ, bidding open about 20 minutes, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer sends only a new end time two hours from now (no start time, no increase_auction_time).
2. Read the round back.
expectedResult: Expected (today): HTTP 200 but the round's end does not move — bid_end_time on its own is neither a reschedule nor an extension. Should be refused (code 2) or applied.
rationale: A buyer (or Clara/an integration) that 'extends' by sending bid_end_time gets a success while vendors are still cut off at the old time.

title: QA_Platform_started_technical_round_cannot_be_rescheduled
preconditions: A fresh live RFP+RFQ event; both rounds started at publish; QA vendor 1 invited to both.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to move the technical (RFP) round to start in one hour and end in two hours.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'. The evaluator step that runs first for technical rounds only acts when forms are sent, so nothing is written.
rationale: Technical rounds take a slightly different path (evaluator handling, closed allowed); the started rule must still hold.

title: QA_Platform_closed_technical_round_cannot_be_rescheduled
preconditions: A fresh RFP+RFQ event whose technical response is in and whose windows are both over.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to move the closed technical round to a new window in the future.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!' — technical rounds stay editable after close (closed is an allowed status for RFP), so the started rule is what stops it.
rationale: Re-opening a finished technical round by 'rescheduling' it would wipe the evaluation timeline; extensions have their own reopen rules.

title: QA_Platform_closed_pricing_round_cannot_be_rescheduled
preconditions: A fresh RFQ whose bidding window and extra closing time are over; QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to move the closed round to a new window in the future.
expectedResult: Refused (HTTP 422): code 4 'Request not found' once the round's status is closed (RFQ rounds are not editable when closed), or code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!' if the close worker has not flipped the status yet.
rationale: A closed commercial round must never be reopened through the reschedule path.

title: QA_Platform_awarded_round_cannot_be_rescheduled
preconditions: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid, the round closed, and an award proposal was created and submitted.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to move the awarded round to a new window in the future.
expectedResult: Refused (HTTP 422): code 769 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.' where the company has rfx projects on (a submitted proposal restricts RFQ changes), otherwise code 4 'Request not found' (closed) or 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.
rationale: Moving the clock of an awarded round would orphan the award.

title: QA_Platform_reschedule_unknown_round
preconditions: Signed-in QA buyer; no event needed.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to reschedule a round id that does not exist.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (the id decodes to 999999999, no such round).
rationale: Bogus ids must fail closed before any policy or schedule logic.

title: QA_Platform_reschedule_garbled_round_id
preconditions: Signed-in QA buyer; no event needed.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to reschedule using a garbled round id.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (the id decodes to nothing, find_by_id(nil) is nil).
rationale: A garbled id must not crash the lookup.

title: QA_Platform_staggered_time_on_draft_round_not_found
preconditions: A fresh draft event with an RFQ round that is not published.
steps: 1. The buyer sends per-line times for one line (start in 1 minute, end in 10 minutes).
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — only rounds in status active are looked up, so a draft is invisible here.
rationale: staggered_time has no permission check of its own; the only thing standing between a caller and the schedule is this lookup, so it must hold in every state.

title: QA_Platform_staggered_time_on_closed_round_not_found
preconditions: A fresh RFQ whose bidding window and extra closing time are over; no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer sends per-line times for one line (start in 1 minute, end in 10 minutes).
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — either the round is no longer active, or it is not a staggered round; both answer 4.
rationale: staggered_time has no permission check of its own; the only thing standing between a caller and the schedule is this lookup, so it must hold in every state.

title: QA_Platform_staggered_time_on_technical_round_refused

rationale: staggered_time has no permission check of its own; the only thing standing between a caller and the schedule is this lookup, so it must hold in every state.

title: QA_Platform_staggered_time_on_awarded_round_refused
preconditions: A fresh RFQ with QA vendor 1's bid, closed, award proposal submitted.
steps: 1. The buyer sends per-line times for one line (start in 1 minute, end in 10 minutes).

rationale: staggered_time has no permission check of its own; the only thing standing between a caller and the schedule is this lookup, so it must hold in every state.

title: QA_Platform_reopen_lines_with_null_line_list_crashes
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered); QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
steps: 1. The buyer asks to reopen lines, sending the line list as null and a 10-minute extension.
expectedResult: Should be refused cleanly (422 code 2, or code 4 for a round that is not staggered). Today the id decoding that runs before every action calls .map on null for any key ending in 'uuids' (params_auth.rb:72-73) and the request fails with HTTP 500 before the controller runs.
rationale: trade_product_uuids is the exact key the Reopen Line Items drawer sends; a null from a bad client must not be a server error.

title: QA_Platform_reopen_lines_on_non_staggered_round_not_found
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. The buyer has create permission (the permission check that runs first passes).
steps: 1. The buyer asks to reopen one line for 10 minutes on a normal (not staggered) live RFQ.
expectedResult: Refused: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — reopening exists only on staggered line-item auctions.
rationale: reopen_line_items had no case at all; these pin its guard order (create permission, then own-company active round, then staggered, then parameters) on states the run can build.

title: QA_Platform_vendor_cannot_bid_after_end_pulled_in
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. counter_offer_modification_enabled is OFF on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time).
steps: 1. The buyer sends an extension whose new end is 90 seconds from now (earlier than the current end).
2. Wait until that new end has passed.
3. QA vendor 1 tries to place a bid.
4. Read the round back.
expectedResult: Step 1 is accepted (Expected today — nothing stops an 'extension' to an earlier time, which cuts ~18 minutes off the vendors' window). Step 3 is refused: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'. The read-back shows the bid end in the past.
rationale: Vendors plan their quote around the published end; the extension field can silently shorten it, and the bid lock-out follows the new clock.

plan.dependsOnSetting: counter_offer_modification_enabled is OFF on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time)

act.say: The buyer moves the bid end IN to 90 seconds from now (an 'extension' to an earlier time).
Wait until the new (earlier) bid end has passed.
QA vendor 1 tries to bid after the new end.

title: QA_Platform_draft_opened_before_end_pulled_in_cannot_be_priced
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
steps: 1. QA vendor 1 opens a draft bid while bidding is open.
2. The buyer moves the bid end in to 90 seconds from now.
3. Wait until that end has passed.
4. QA vendor 1 tries to price the line on the draft it opened in step 1.
expectedResult: Step 4 is refused (HTTP 422): code 32 'Bid not found' once the end-of-bidding job has discarded drafts, otherwise code 33 'Order not active' (or 508 'Not allowed to bid on this product' where counter-offer modification is on and the round is in its extra closing time).
rationale: A vendor half-way through a quote when the clock is pulled in must not be able to finish it after the new end.

act.say: QA vendor 1 opens a draft bid while bidding is open.
The buyer moves the bid end IN to 90 seconds from now (an 'extension' to an earlier time).
Wait until the new (earlier) bid end has passed.
QA vendor 1 tries to price its draft after the new end.

title: QA_Platform_vendor_cannot_revise_after_end_pulled_in
preconditions: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; bidding still open. counter_offer_modification_enabled is OFF on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time).
steps: 1. The buyer moves the bid end in to 90 seconds from now.
2. Wait until that end has passed.
3. QA vendor 1 tries to revise (place a new bid).
expectedResult: Step 3 is refused: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'. The earlier submitted bid stays the vendor's quote.
rationale: Revisions follow the moved clock too; a vendor that already quoted must not slip a better price in after the new end.
